_readme: Subjects for SF Times features. status: open | researching | drafted | published | dropped. The morning task takes the lowest-numbered open subjects. A subject that fails the source-quality floor is marked dropped with a reason, never silently retried, so the same dead end is not researched twice.

topics.subject: Kevin Chan / Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory, Ross Alley
topics.note: the last operation in Chinatown still folding fortune cookies by hand, one at a time, in a tiny alley shop.
topics.dropped_reason: Researched 2026-09-09. Every retrievable source was travel-guide or listicle content; zero load-bearing. Needs real reporting or a primary source before it can be revisited.

topics.subject: SF Neon (Randall Ann Homan & Al Barna)
topics.note: the two people documenting and saving the city's vanishing neon signs before the last of them go dark.

topics.subject: The caretaker of the San Francisco Columbarium
topics.note: who restored the domed Neptune Society building and can tell you the story inside almost every niche.

topics.subject: Dan Zelinsky / Musée Mécanique
topics.note: keeper of one of the world's largest collections of working antique coin-operated arcade machines, at Fisherman's Wharf.

topics.subject: The cable car bell-ringers
topics.note: the grip operators who compete in the annual Cable Car Bell Ringing Contest, and what the craft of ringing actually is.

topics.subject: Aileen Barr, Colette Crutcher & the 16th Avenue Tiled Steps volunteers
topics.note: the mosaic artists and neighbors who turned a staircase into one of the city's most-photographed public artworks, and who maintain it.

topics.subject: The Guerrilla Grafters
topics.note: activists quietly grafting fruit-bearing branches onto San Francisco's ornamental city trees so the sidewalks feed people.

topics.subject: The Prelinger Library
topics.note: Rick and Megan Prelinger's open, browsable private archive of American ephemera in SoMa, organized by geography, free to anyone.

topics.subject: The Bay Area's community fridge network
topics.note: the volunteer-run "town fridges" that became a mutual-aid movement, and the people who keep them stocked.

topics.subject: The Free Farm Stand / urban agriculture in the Mission
topics.note: free-produce initiatives and the volunteers growing and giving away food in the city.

topics.subject: The tool-lending libraries of Oakland and Berkeley
topics.note: borrow a table saw like a library book, one of the oldest such programs in the country.

topics.subject: Friends of the Urban Forest
topics.note: the volunteer movement planting and defending San Francisco's street trees, block by block.

topics.subject: The Marine Mammal Center, Marin Headlands
topics.note: the hospital that rescues and rehabs seals and sea lions across 600 miles of California coast, mostly on volunteer labor.

topics.subject: 826 Valencia & the Pirate Supply Store
topics.note: the youth writing nonprofit hidden behind a joke storefront, and how the gag funds the tutoring.

topics.subject: Creativity Explored / NIAD
topics.note: the studios giving artists with developmental disabilities a real professional practice and gallery career.

topics.subject: Glide or St. Anthony's
topics.note: the free-meals institutions of the Tenderloin, the scale of what they serve, and who keeps the kitchens running.

topics.subject: Larkin Street Youth Services
topics.note: the organization catching San Francisco's homeless and runaway young people, and how the model works.

topics.subject: Roots Community Health Center, Oakland
topics.note: Dr. Noha Aboelata's model for Black community health and street medicine in the East Bay.

topics.subject: The Mission mural movement
topics.note: Precita Eyes, Balmy Alley, Clarion Alley, and the muralists keeping the city's most political public-art tradition alive.

topics.subject: D'Arcy Drollinger, SF's Drag Laureate & Oasis
topics.note: the nation's first official city drag laureate and the drag renaissance behind the appointment.

topics.subject: Carnaval San Francisco
topics.note: the Mission's decades-old Latin and Caribbean street festival, its origins, and the organizers who sustain it.

topics.subject: Bay Area lowrider culture
topics.note: the Mission cruising tradition, its suppression and revival, and the clubs carrying it forward.

topics.subject: City Lights and the living Beat legacy
topics.note: the bookstore-as-institution after Ferlinghetti, run now by Elaine Katzenberger, and why it still matters.

topics.subject: The Bay's turntablism and hip-hop lineage
topics.note: from Invisibl Skratch Piklz to hyphy, the region's outsized influence and who carries it now.

topics.subject: Audium
topics.note: Stan Shaff's sound-sculpture theater, 176 speakers in total darkness, running near Sutro since the 1970s.

topics.subject: The Wave Organ
topics.note: the tide-powered acoustic sculpture on a jetty in the bay, and the physics and history behind it.

topics.subject: The Institute of Illegal Images (Mark McCloud)
topics.note: the world's largest archive of LSD blotter art, treated as a serious folk-art collection, in a Mission Victorian.

topics.subject: The Camera Obscura at Ocean Beach
topics.note: the "Giant Camera" projecting the live sea onto a disc, a Cliff House survivor and its keepers.

topics.subject: The Seward Street Slides
topics.note: the concrete slides a teenager designed in the 1970s, still ridden on flattened cardboard today.

topics.subject: The Interval / Long Now Foundation
topics.note: the 10,000-year clock, Brian Eno's involvement, and long-term thinking as a Bay Area cultural project, at Fort Mason.
